title: Describing motion; Motion graphs; Constant-acceleration equations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: K01-1#N.2, K03-1#N.5a, K01-1#N.5, K03-1#N.12, K01-1#N.10, K03-1#N.16.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity, in m s⁻².

items.label: Displacement
items.clue: The change in position: a vector quantity.

items.label: Average speed
items.clue: Whole path length divided by whole time taken: a scalar.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: Total length of the path: a scalar that is never negative.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?
A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?

An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.

questions.stem: A student drops a ball from rest from several heights h and times each fall, t. She plots t² (y-axis) against h (x-axis): a straight line through the origin with gradient 0.204 s² m⁻¹. What value of g do the results give?
questions.explanation: h = ½gt² gives t² = (2/g)h, so the gradient is 2/g. g = 2 ÷ 0.204 = 9.80 m s⁻².

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A toy car is released from rest on a straight slope and speeds up with constant acceleration. It travels 0.60 m in the first 2.0 s. How far does it travel between t = 4.0 s and t = 6.0 s?
